text.p: These are the leading stories in Zambia's press on Monday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- A former senior Zambia Conolidated Copper Mines (ZCCM) executive claims that a small group of executives are swindling the company through dubious supply and transportation contracts with South African firms.
- The Zambian National Union of Teachers claims the opposition is using some teachers in a civil disobedience campaign to agitate for industrial action.
- The government records a budget surplus in the second quarter of 1997 after a deficit in the first quarter.
- The Zambia Electricity Supply Corp says new owners of ZCCM will have to pay 75 percent more for power because the state-run corporations will not subsidise private companies.
- The capital's local authority sets fire to illegal street vendors' stalls in the city centre.
